From 97d5c8f5c09a604c4873c8348f58de3cea69a7df Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Tomasz=20Paku=C5=82a?= <tomasz.pakula.oficjalny@gmail.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Feb 2026 22:44:55 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] HID: pidff: Fix condition effect bit clearing
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

As reported by MPDarkGuy on discord, NULL pointer dereferences were
happening because not all the conditional effects bits were cleared.

Properly clear all conditional effect bits from ffbit

Fixes: 7f3d7bc0df4b ("HID: pidff: Better quirk assigment when searching for fields")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org # 6.18.x
Signed-off-by: Tomasz Pakuła <tomasz.pakula.oficjalny@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Jiri Kosina <jkosina@suse.com>

diff --git a/drivers/hid/usbhid/hid-pidff.c b/drivers/hid/usbhid/hid-pidff.c
index a4e700b40ba9..56d6af39ba81 100644
--- a/drivers/hid/usbhid/hid-pidff.c
+++ b/drivers/hid/usbhid/hid-pidff.c
@@ -1452,10 +1452,13 @@ static int pidff_init_fields(struct pidff_device *pidff, struct input_dev *dev)
 		hid_warn(pidff->hid, "unknown ramp effect layout\n");
 
 	if (PIDFF_FIND_FIELDS(set_condition, PID_SET_CONDITION, 1)) {
-		if (test_and_clear_bit(FF_SPRING, dev->ffbit)   ||
-		    test_and_clear_bit(FF_DAMPER, dev->ffbit)   ||
-		    test_and_clear_bit(FF_FRICTION, dev->ffbit) ||
-		    test_and_clear_bit(FF_INERTIA, dev->ffbit))
+		bool test = false;
+
+		test |= test_and_clear_bit(FF_SPRING, dev->ffbit);
+		test |= test_and_clear_bit(FF_DAMPER, dev->ffbit);
+		test |= test_and_clear_bit(FF_FRICTION, dev->ffbit);
+		test |= test_and_clear_bit(FF_INERTIA, dev->ffbit);
+		if (test)
 			hid_warn(pidff->hid, "unknown condition effect layout\n");
 	}
 
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Modifications

### Modified File: `drivers/hid/usbhid/hid-pidff.c`

**Change Description:**  
The patch fixes a bug where conditional effect bits were not fully cleared due to short-circuit evaluation in the original code. The original `if` statement used the logical OR operator (`||`) which stops evaluating as soon as a true result is found, leaving the remaining bits uncleared. This caused null pointer dereferences when some conditional effects were still marked as supported but their associated fields were missing.

**Specific Modification:**  
- A boolean variable `test` is introduced to accumulate the results of `test_and_clear_bit()` for each of the four conditional effect bits (`FF_SPRING`, `FF_DAMPER`, `FF_FRICTION`, `FF_INERTIA`).  
- Instead of directly using the bit operations inside the `if` condition, each bit is now unconditionally cleared using `|=` assignment, ensuring all four bits are always cleared.  
- The warning message is then only issued if any of the bits were actually set (i.e., `test` is true).

### Relationships Between Modifications

The change is self-contained within a single file and directly addresses the root cause of the bug:  
- **Before fix:** The short-circuit evaluation meant that when multiple condition effect bits were set, only the first one that was found and cleared would be processed, leaving the others uncleared. This inconsistency led to null pointer dereferences later in the code when those uncleared bits referenced missing fields.  
- **After fix:** All four conditional effect bits are always cleared in sequence, guaranteeing that the device’s `ffbit` mask is correctly updated regardless of the order or number of bits set. This prevents the null pointer dereference by ensuring no stale bits remain active.

Root cause:
The original code used logical OR (||) inside the if condition to clear conditional effect bits. Due to short-circuit evaluation, once `test_and_clear_bit` returned true for the first bit, the remaining bits were not tested or cleared. This left some condition effect bits uncleared, causing null pointer dereferences later when those bits referenced missing fields.

Code statements information:
The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
if (test_and_clear_bit(FF_SPRING, dev->ffbit)   ||
    test_and_clear_bit(FF_DAMPER, dev->ffbit)   ||
    test_and_clear_bit(FF_FRICTION, dev->ffbit) ||
    test_and_clear_bit(FF_INERTIA, dev->ffbit))
```
Reason:
The original condition uses logical OR (`||`) which employs short-circuit evaluation. As soon as the first `test_and_clear_bit` returns true, the remaining calls are skipped. This leaves some conditional effect bits (FF_DAMPER, FF_FRICTION, FF_INERTIA) uncleared in `dev->ffbit`, causing later code to attempt to use missing fields and trigger null pointer dereferences.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
bool test = false;

test |= test_and_clear_bit(FF_SPRING, dev->ffbit);
test |= test_and_clear_bit(FF_DAMPER, dev->ffbit);
test |= test_and_clear_bit(FF_FRICTION, dev->ffbit);
test |= test_and_clear_bit(FF_INERTIA, dev->ffbit);
if (test)
```
Reason:
The fix ensures all four `test_and_clear_bit` calls are executed regardless of their return values by using a boolean variable and `|=` assignment. This guarantees that every conditional effect bit is properly cleared (or tested) before checking if any of them were set. The warning is then issued only if at least one bit was cleared, avoiding the short-circuit problem and preventing the null pointer dereferences.
